description: Golden-signals view of the distributed Loki deployment (latency, traffic, errors, saturation; drill-downs collapsed below). Replaces the gnetId-17781 community dashboard. Every query is validated against live Mimir by scripts/check-dashboard-queries.py.

panels.title: Components Up
panels.description: All 10 single-replica Loki components plus the two memcached pods. Anything below 10 is an outage.

panels.title: Error % (1h)
panels.description: 5xx/error share of all requests across every component, health-check and internal long-poll routes excluded.

panels.title: Panics (24h)
panels.description: Recovered panics across all components. Non-zero means a component is hitting a code path that crashes.

panels.title: Compactor Run Age
panels.description: Time since the last successful index compaction. A stalled compactor silently bloats the TSDB index and S3 until queries die.

panels.title: Discarded Lines/s
panels.description: Log lines Loki rejected (rate limits, age, line size). This is data loss the producers never see.

panels.title: Write p99
panels.description: Push-path p99 on the distributor. Backpressure signal for every Alloy and Jenkins-master producer.

panels.title: Read p99
panels.description: Query-frontend p99 over the user-facing query routes. What Grafana Explore users actually feel.

panels.title: Ingest Throughput
panels.description: Decompressed bytes accepted by the distributor. The demand baseline: drops mean producers broke, spikes explain everything else.

panels.title: Ingest Lines/s
panels.description: Log lines accepted by the distributor. Diverging from byte rate distinguishes more logs from bigger logs.

panels.title: Write latency (push)
panels.description: Distributor push-route latency. A p50/p99 spread means tail-only slowness (one slow ingester flush); all three moving together is systemic.

panels.title: Read latency by route (frontend)
panels.description: Per-route p99 on the query frontend. query_range vs labels vs series fail differently (chunk fetch vs index); the split localizes read pain.

panels.title: Request p99 by component
panels.description: Request p99 per component, noise routes excluded. With one replica per component, the slow hop names itself.

panels.title: Ingest throughput
panels.description: Bytes and lines accepted at the distributor. Bytes-and-lines together date capacity discussions and catch runaway producers.

panels.title: API request rate by route
panels.description: Write QPS (distributor) and read QPS (frontend) on user-facing surfaces only. The demand side of every latency or error change.

panels.title: Error ratio (write / read / overall)
panels.description: The two SLOs that matter (can producers push, can users query) plus the all-component ratio.

panels.title: Non-2xx responses by status code
panels.description: 429 (rate limit) vs 400 (bad payload) vs 5xx demand completely different fixes.

panels.title: Discarded log lines by reason
panels.description: Names the exact limit eating data (rate_limited, too_far_behind, line_too_long, greater_than_max_sample_age). Maps 1:1 to a limits-config fix.

panels.title: Ring health (non-ACTIVE members)
panels.description: Flat zero when healthy. Any blip is the memberlist/ring pathology that has previously wedged this stack (see ADR 0014).

panels.title: PVC utilization
panels.description: Ingester WAL and compactor volumes. A full disk is the hard-stop failure for ingest.

panels.title: Query scheduler queue
panels.description: THE read-saturation signal with a single querier: inflight growth and queue wait precede user-visible read latency. (Loki exposes no queue-length gauge; inflight is the scheduler's saturation summary.)

panels.title: Ingester streams & chunks in memory
panels.description: Stream cardinality is the ingester's memory ceiling. A label-cardinality explosion from a Jenkins job shows up here first.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Read-latency regressions are usually cache-miss regressions. Client-side vs memcached-side ratios disambiguate eviction from key-shape problems.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (job) (rate(memcached_commands_total{namespace="loki", command="get", status="hit"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (job) (rate(memcached_commands_total{namespace="loki", command="get"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Index read latency p99
panels.description: Separates index-lookup slowness from chunk-fetch slowness, the two halves of every slow LogQL query.

panels.title: Flush & WAL operations
panels.description: Flush reasons explain chunk quality; failures and WAL errors are the only early warnings before the ingester loses data.

panels.title: Chunk size & compression at flush
panels.description: Tiny chunks mean stream-cardinality misconfiguration (S3 cost, slow reads). Tuning feedback for chunk_idle_period and chunk_target_size.

panels.title: Chunk age at flush
panels.description: Age at flush vs max_chunk_age shows whether flushes are time-forced (healthy) or memory-forced (pressure).

panels.title: S3 request rate by operation
panels.description: Object-store trouble cascades into everything. The error overlay separates S3-side failures from Loki-side ones.

panels.title: S3 latency p99 by operation
panels.description: Distinguishes S3 throttling or slowness from Loki-side slowness when reads or flushes degrade.

panels.title: Index maintenance ages
panels.description: Three sawtooth lines that should never climb. Retention silently not running is an S3-cost incident (ADR 0015).

panels.title: RSS & goroutines by component
panels.description: Goroutine leaks precede OOMs. One panel replaces the old dashboard's eleven Go runtime panels.

panels.title: CPU vs requests per pod
panels.description: Sized against requests because the loki pods set no CPU limits. Sustained >100% is burst-headroom theft; bump requests.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace="loki", container!="", container!="POD"}[$__rate_interval])) / on (pod) group_left() sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace="loki", resource="cpu"})

panels.title: Memory working set vs limit per pod
panels.description: Distance to OOMKill per pod.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="loki", container!="", container!="POD"}) / on (pod) group_left() sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace="loki", resource="memory"})

title: Loki / Golden Signals
